explanation: No clear shared feature: fires on assorted tokens in the middle of code (punctuation such as ), ::, "). , ==, quote marks) and in prose in many languages (word-pieces, contractions, function words). The token and its surroundings give no consistent signal.

Fires on the word right after a superlative or 'first/ever/never' phrase that marks a record or first occurrence ('first [title]', 'first [woman]', 'ever [eaten]', 'has never [tried]', 'all-time record [for]', 'first reported case [of]', 'the [oldest]'). It fires more weakly on 'report the [case]' and on purpose-'to' after a description of a study or device. Context matters most: the same noun with no first/superlative framing gets little activation.

Fires on fragments inside dense technical notation or mid-word subword pieces: numbers and symbols inside LaTeX fractions or exponents, array indices, regex pieces, and the second piece of split biomedical words or names ('ant'iviral, 'pl'asminogen, 'ri-bose', Pl-asmodium). It is a loose 'token in the middle of a fragmented technical string' detector, not one concept.

Fires on the word naming the result or product of an earlier process, or a time after it: 'the [trained] weights', 'return [result]', 'look at the [results]', 'post[operative]', 'with the [new] values', 'the [created] user', 'money [from] the sale', 'After [treatment]'. Strongest where the context sets up a before/after sequence and the token points to the outcome or aftermath.

Fires on tokens inside stock discourse phrases that frame or introduce the next point: 'to [name] a few', 'To [add] to that', 'One [thing] is certain', 'That['s]', 'First [off]', 'What['s] more', 'On [top] of', 'The best [part]', 'All [that] said', 'As far [as]'. Fires on the key word of such a phrase, usually at the start of a sentence; ordinary uses of the same words fire weakly.

Fires on predictable tokens in formulaic boilerplate: software license headers ('Licensed under the Apache [License]', 'must reproduce [the] above copyright', 'MIT [license]'), privacy notices, and standard code or markup idioms ('type="[text]/javascript"', 'apply-[templates]', '-[ms]-transform'), plus templated math word problems. In short, it fires on the expected next token of highly stereotyped templated text.

Two jobs: (1) end-of-statement tokens in code, mainly ';' or ';\n' / '();\n' closing Java/C#/ObjC statements and import lines; (2) verb forms in Russian and other Slavic/Romance text, especially 'быть'/'будет' after modal 'может'. Code statement terminators are the most consistent trigger.

Fires on the token just before a ' : ' separator: the true branch of a ternary ('? [a] :', '? [true] :'), keys in key : value pairs written with a space before the colon, C++ initializer or inheritance colons ('Cow(int age[)] : Animal'), and padding before ':' in legal caption layouts. Strongest when the next token is a spaced colon in code; scattered weak French and other prose hits.

Fires on nouns (often word-final pieces) from combat sports, martial arts and blades or sports gear: WBO, Street Fighter, Kung Fu, MMA, UFC, flyweight, knife/knives, blades, scabbard, razors, snowboard, skates, skis. Strongest on combat-sport and weapon terms; weaker on other sport or equipment words and on name endings.

Fires on a token that starts or continues a camel-case or abbreviation identifier inside code or citation strings, especially the capital letter or piece after a prefix or separator: NS[S]ecureCoding, NST[imeInterval], [F]Sharp, _Q[STRINGBUILDER], check[C]udaErrors, M.S[.P].R., RM[SS]D, -b[cm]. Code identifiers and acronym fragments give the strongest response.

Two jobs: (1) the auxiliary or verb right after a subject in present-perfect or news-lead sentences, especially 'has/have [been]' (also 'has [been] booked', 'We've [improved]', 'engine [was]'); (2) digits and hyphens inside legal and patent docket or citation numbers (case 'No. WR-17,5[7]5', '2016[-]Ohio', 'Pat. Nos. 4,46[6]'). The two jobs show up as separate clusters.

No coherent pattern: fires on commas between function parameters in code, years inside copyright lines, spaces in citations, Vietnamese 'thể', 'I [came] across', and assorted word-pieces. Code argument separators recur, but much of the activation is unrelated.

Fires on the start of a temporal expression that follows an event verb, marking when something happens or happened: 'next' (week/year/month/Christmas), 'this' Friday/week, 'last' night, 'within' 15 years, 'in' (year), 'a few' hours, 'as early as', 'over' centuries. Strongest on 'next' after a planned action; locative or other prepositions fire only weakly.

Fires in code at assignment and initialization of fields or variables inside a method or constructor body: the '=' or '||=' in 'x = ...', or the target-start token ('@', 'this', 'm', '$this->', 'a1_('). Strongest at the first assignment statement on a new indented line; weak on license boilerplate and prose.
